extracted.intended_audience: individual scholars, independent researchers, and writers preparing an application to the NEH Public Scholar Program
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit an application for an NEH Public Scholar award to support writing a well-researched humanities book (or book-plus-digital materials) for a broad general readership. Includes eligibility, required application components, formatting rules, evaluation criteria, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project audience and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports well-researched books in the humanities intended to reach a broad readership; projects that are directed primarily to scholars are not appropriate for this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such scholarship might present narrative history, tell stories of important individuals, analyze significant texts, provide syntheses, revive interest in neglected subjects, or examine the latest thinking on a topic. The application should explain how the project will appeal to general readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding in humanities research
rubrics_metrics.description: Books supported must be grounded in humanities research and scholarship, making appropriate use of primary and/or secondary sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the project’s scholarly basis in the narrative and show the breadth and depth of humanities research underlying the project (see evaluation criterion 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible writing style for general readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must promise a manuscript written in a readily accessible style that addresses significant humanities themes in a way that will appeal to a large audience of general readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative should not assume specialized knowledge and should be free of technical terms and jargon; writing sample must demonstrate how the final product will read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible project types
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects or uses explicitly not allowed for Public Scholar awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH Public Scholar awards may not be used for: promotion of a particular political, religious, or ideological point of view; advocacy of a particular program of social or political action; support of specific public policies or legislation; projects that fall outside of the humanities (including creation/performance of art; creative writing, memoirs, creative nonfiction; empirically based social science research or policy studies); research for doctoral dissertations or theses by students enrolled in a degree program; dissertation revision projects; preparation or revision of textbooks; curriculum development; development of teaching methods or theories; educational or technical impact assessments; historical fiction and philosophical novels; guide books, how-to books, self-help books; anthologies and edited collections of essays; publications consisting primarily of transcribed interviews, oral histories, or questionnaire responses; projects devoted primarily to promoting or disseminating a completed book; books for children or young adults; works of graphic fiction or nonfiction; translations (and others listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed products and public access preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Supported products might be printed books (paperback or hardbound), e-books, audiobooks, or in all these formats; digital or Web-based products intended to supplement a proposed book are also allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All other considerations equal, NEH gives preference to products the public can access at no cost. Grantees agree NEH (in consultation with publishers) may post excerpts on the NEH website and/or in Humanities magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award duration and stipend calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards support continuous work over six to twelve months; awards may be held part time or full time; stipend is $4,200 per full-time month with a maximum stipend of $50,400 for a twelve-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards will be reduced to reflect smaller time commitments; recipients must work at least half-time and the equivalent of at least six full-time months. No grant may exceed twelve months. Requesting a shorter award period will not improve chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work expectations during award
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients working full-time must forgo other major activities, including teaching; recipients combining a part-time award with teaching must carry a reduced class load during the award period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should request award periods that suit their schedules and projects. Recipients who work full-time must not undertake major outside commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing, indirect costs, and budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Scholar awards go to individuals, do not require cost sharing, and do not include indirect costs; because award amounts are determined by time commitment, no budget is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful applicants must complete the Public Scholar Acceptance Form, from which payment amounts will be determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship and residency eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. citizens (inside or outside U.S.) are eligible; foreign nationals who have been living in the United States or its jurisdictions for at least three years prior to the application deadline are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must indicate citizenship on Form I; follow instructions for entering ZIP/postal codes and congressional district information as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication record eligibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible, applicants must either: (a) have written as sole author a book published by a university or commercial press; OR (b) have written at least three articles and essays appearing in publications that reach a large national or international audience of general readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles/essays may be print or electronic. Applicants may not meet this requirement with a co-authored volume, an edited collection/anthology, a self-published book, a book not yet published, or articles in peer-reviewed academic journals or publications aimed primarily at professional readers. List relevant publications on the résumé.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currently enrolled students and dissertation restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals currently enrolled in a degree-granting program are ineligible; applicants may not request funding for projects based on completed dissertations or for dissertation revision projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants unable to meet publication requirements may consider NEH Fellowships or Summer Stipends instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously NEH-supported projects and prior awards
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not apply for funding for a project previously supported by an NEH Fellowship, a Public Scholar award, or an Award for Faculty; you may apply for a project previously supported by a two-month NEH Summer Stipend (with evaluators reviewing previous accomplishments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An NEH grant for one stage does not commit NEH to continued support for later stages; applications for each stage are evaluated independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent grants and multiple applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may simultaneously hold fellowships or grants from institutions other than NEH in support of the same project during the award period and may have a publisher advance; applicants may submit only one Public Scholar proposal per year but may compete concurrently in listed NEH/partner programs; applicants may hold or accept only one NEH individual award in a given federal fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking funding for a co-author each person must submit a separate application; collaborative awards are not divisible (see collaborative projects guidance). Consult FAQs for sequencing restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative project rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is designed primarily for individual researchers; awards may not be divided. Co-authors must each submit separate applications specifying individual contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each application will be evaluated on its own merits; applications should explain division of labor and dependencies. Applicants seeking funding only for themselves but working in a team should explain the division. Consider NEH Collaborative Research grant for larger collaborative projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion: appeal and intellectual significance for general readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators judge the appeal and intellectual significance of the proposed book for general readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative should describe why the topic matters and why it will interest general readers; explain scope, basic ideas, problems, questions, texts, people, and events the book will explore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion: applicant's record of interpreting humanities for general audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators assess the applicant’s record of research and experience in interpreting the humanities for general audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Résumé, publications, prior awards, and letters of recommendation should document experience conveying scholarship to broad audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion: quality of conception, organization, and research
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators assess the quality of the conception, definition, organization, and description of the project and the breadth and depth of the humanities research underlying it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative should include chapter outline and describe research materials and methodology to demonstrate project conception and scholarly foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion: quality of the writing sample and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators judge the quality of the writing sample and the applicant’s clarity of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing sample should demonstrate how the final product will read and the applicant’s ability to write effectively for a broad audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion: feasibility, dissemination, and likelihood of completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators assess the feasibility and appropriateness of the proposed plan of work, the soundness of the dissemination plan, and the likelihood that the applicant will complete the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a realistic work plan with schedule, months requested, full- or part-time status, and dissemination/marketing plans (and publisher arrangements if any).

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: length, formatting, and required content areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative must not exceed four single-spaced pages and should provide an intellectual justification addressing: significance and contribution; work plan; competencies, skills, and access; and final product and dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use one-inch margins, font no smaller than eleven point. Images, charts, diagrams, footnotes, and endnotes are allowed if they fit within the four-page limit. The narrative should not assume specialized knowledge and should avoid jargon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: significance and contribution content
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the significance and appeal of the proposed project for general audiences; explain why the topic matters and provide an overview of scope and basic ideas to be explored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss the project’s scholarly basis and how that scholarship will be conveyed to general audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: work plan content and chapter outline
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe research and specify the part or stage of the project to be supported; indicate completed parts, provide a work plan with schedule, and include a chapter outline with brief indications of each chapter’s contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate months of support requested and whether full- or part-time (or a combination); such detail is especially important when chapter titles are not self-explanatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: competencies, skills, and access content
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain competence in the project area and experience in conveying scholarship to broad audiences; specify language or skill competence needed and arrangements for access to archives, collections, or institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If subject is new to you, explain reasons and qualifications; describe where study will be conducted and primary/secondary materials used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: final product and dissemination content
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how you will couch the book’s contents to appeal to a broad audience; describe intended audiences, timing for submission and publication, and dissemination/marketing plans with publisher if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing digital/electronic/Web-based supplements, discuss their technical specifications and explain how they will be supported and maintained beyond the grant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliography must not exceed one single-spaced page and should consist of primary and/or secondary sources that relate directly to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators use the bibliography to assess knowledge of the subject area and methodology. Any standard bibliographic format is acceptable. Items referenced in the narrative need not appear in the bibliography if the narrative citation enables identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Résumé requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Résumé must not exceed two single-spaced pages and must include current and past positions, education (degrees, dates, titles of theses/dissertations), awards/honors (with dates), publications (full citations), and other relevant professional activities and accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include level of competence in relevant foreign languages and indicate prior NEH support with dates and resulting publications. Do not submit a narrative biographical statement in place of the résumé.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing sample requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a writing sample of not more than twenty double-spaced pages (including footnotes/endnotes); single-space notes if desired. Best to provide a draft chapter or a partial chapter; if unavailable, a writing sample in the style of the proposed book is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample should be no more than five years old, demonstrate how the final product will read, may not include more than one work or excerpts from more than one work, and may not include a table of contents, outline, or abstract of the proposed book. Visual materials are permitted if they fit within the limit. If using a PDF of prior publication pages, length must not exceed equivalent of 20 double-spaced pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher’s letter of interest or commitment (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with explored publication arrangements are encouraged to submit a letter from an official representative of a publisher indicating physical formats planned, dissemination plans, and print-run expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not substitute or include a book contract. Publisher may provide a letter of commitment/interest but should not submit a letter of recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are asked to solicit two letters of reference that speak directly to the evaluation criteria and the applicant’s ability to write effectively for a broad audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide names, e-mail addresses, and affiliations for two referees on Form III (one e-mail each). NEH will e-mail requests to letter writers ~7–10 days after the deadline; letters must be submitted online no later than the specified deadline (Feb 28, 2018). Applicants are responsible for ensuring referees receive and submit letters. Missing letters will not disqualify an application, but late letters may not be considered by evaluators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments: format, order, and filenames
rubrics_metrics.description: All component parts must be attached as PDFs in the Attachments Form using specified attachment slots, order, and exact filenames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachment 1: narrative.pdf; Attachment 2: bibliography.pdf; Attachment 3: resume.pdf; Attachment 4: writingsample.pdf; Attachment 5: publisherletter.pdf (if applicable). Requirements: attachments must be PDF; must be in specified order; must use specified names; must not exceed length limits; no other attachments may be included. Do not use accented characters in filenames.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form III supplemental information and reference details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide field(s) of project, project director field of study, address info (home or work), institutional affiliation (including DUNS and TIN/EIN for U.S. institutions), status (junior vs senior scholar), and names/emails/affiliations of two recommenders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not affiliated, indicate No and continue. Applicants with U.S. affiliation must include institutional DUNS and TIN/EIN. Status: junior scholar = 7 years or less beyond final degree; senior = 8+ years beyond final degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov registration and account requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be submitted via Grants.gov using an individual Grants.gov account (not an institutional account). NEH recommends completing registration at least two weeks before the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registering as an individual, use Grants.gov individual registration URL and Funding Opportunity Number if prompted. Grants.gov will auto-fill an INDV00000 DUNS-like code—do not change it. Contact Grants.gov help desk for problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process, validation, and confirmation messages
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission to Grants.gov the applicant should receive up to five e-mail messages representing stages: Submission Receipt, Validation Receipt (or rejection with errors), Agency Retrieval Receipt, Agency Tracking Number Assignment (NEH application number), and Agency Notes Assigned (application accepted by NEH) — verify receipt of all five messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Grants.gov or NEH rejects the application for errors, correct and resubmit before the deadline. Use the Grants.gov tracking number in correspondence. If you do not receive all messages, check spam/junk or contact Grants.gov immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline and timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must be received by Grants.gov by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the stated deadline (February 7, 2018). Letters of reference must be submitted online no later than February 28, 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH will not review late, incomplete, or ineligible applications. NEH suggests submitting by 5:00 p.m. ET on the deadline day to allow time to resolve technical problems. You may resubmit corrected versions prior to the deadline; NEH keeps only the most recent submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and format compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that violate format instructions (including page limits) will not be reviewed; NEH will check that attachments are proper PDFs and conform to requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix Grants.gov validation errors and NEH attachment problems and resubmit before the deadline; NEH will email reasons for rejection if attachments are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission tracking of reference letters
rubrics_metrics.description: After the five Grants.gov messages, applicants may check the status of letters by logging into the secure area of NEH’s website using NEH application number and Grants.gov tracking number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can see names and e-mail addresses of letter writers and whether letters have arrived; you may send reminders (including the upload link) from this site. Applicants are responsible for ensuring letter writers submit letters by the due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications receive peer review by knowledgeable persons outside NEH; NEH staff may comment on matters of fact or missing significant issues, then make recommendations to the National Council on the Humanities; the NEH chairman makes all funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More details about NEH’s review process are available on NEH resources. Applicants may request evaluations of their applications after notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award obligations and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Award recipients are expected to participate in public events (keynotes, public lectures, festivals) and must allow NEH (in consultation with publishers) to post excerpts. A final performance report is due within ninety days after the award ending date; a final financial report is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must accept NEH terms set forth in General Information on NEH Public Scholar Program Awards and any award-specific conditions. Instructions for final report submission are available via eGMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application checklist and administrative best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the provided application checklist: verify Grants.gov registration; access package; complete forms I–III; attach required PDFs with exact filenames; upload to Grants.gov; verify five confirmation messages; monitor letters — and adhere to suggested timelines (e.g., register two weeks early).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH strongly suggests early registration and submission to allow time for troubleshooting; Grants.gov help desk is available 7 days/week and applicants should keep tracking numbers and confirmation messages for records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork burden estimate and contact for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH estimates average time to complete the application is fifteen hours per response (includes reviewing instructions, researching, gathering information, completing and reviewing the application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send comments regarding the estimated completion time or other aspects of the application (including suggestions for reducing completion time) to the Chief Guidelines Officer at guidelines@neh.gov (and the OMB Paperwork Reduction Project address provided).
